title: The bill as a monitoring signal: the spike that means an incident

videos.script: Some incidents customers never feel. A debug flag left on. A forgotten load test. Somebody else's miner on your account. The service works, and the only thing that moves is the bill. {{bill}} This lesson makes the bill a signal like any other. A budget with two alerts: one when the money is spent, one when the forecast says it will be. {{budget}} A CloudWatch metric for the bill, and why an alarm on its level fires on the wrong day. {{metric}} Then forty-five days of the shop's costs, and a small program that finds the day the spend changed and the service that moved. Thirty-one dollars a day, all of it logs. That is not a billing question. It is an incident, with a cause. {{spike}} And a warning about every detector built on a recent baseline: after a week, the spike is the new normal. {{normal}} This is the last lesson. The course ends where it should: with the bill noticing first, and a team that hears about it the same day. {{end}}
